title: Near-Earth Objects: The Census
summary: 30,000+ near-Earth asteroids cataloged; an estimated 25,000+ larger than 140m remain unfound.
body:
Civil planetary defense: the real science of protecting Earth from asteroids, comets, and solar storms. NASA's DART mission proved deflection works; surveys map the neighborhood.

title: DART: Humanity's First Deflection
summary: NASA's DART (2022) slammed into Dimorphos at 6 km/s, changing its orbital period by 33 minutes — 25x the success threshold.
body:
NASA's DART (2022) slammed into Dimorphos at 6 km/s, changing its orbital period by 33 minutes — 25x the success threshold. ESA's Hera (2024 launch) will survey the crater. Kinetic impactors work.

title: The Torino Scale
summary: The Torino scale (0-10) communicates impact hazard: 0 = no hazard, 10 = certain global catastrophe.
body:
The Torino scale (0-10) communicates impact hazard: 0 = no hazard, 10 = certain global catastrophe. Apophis briefly hit 4 in 2004 (the record); refined observations retired the risk. Communication is part of defense.

title: Chelyabinsk 2013: The Wake-Up Call
summary: A 20-meter asteroid exploded over Russia with ~500 kilotons of energy — 30x Hiroshima — injuring 1,500 (mostly flying glass).
body:
A 20-meter asteroid exploded over Russia with ~500 kilotons of energy — 30x Hiroshima — injuring 1,500 (mostly flying glass). It arrived undetected, from the sun's direction. The lesson: the sky is not fully watched.

title: Tunguska 1908
summary: A ~50m object flattened 2,150 km^2 of Siberian forest — 80 million trees.
body:
A ~50m object flattened 2,150 km^2 of Siberian forest — 80 million trees. No crater: it airburst. Had it arrived hours later, it would have hit St. Petersburg. The benchmark for regional devastation.

title: Gamma-Ray Bursts: The Distant Threat
summary: GRBs are real and lethal — but the dangerous ones are thousands of light-years away.
body:
GRBs are real and lethal — but the dangerous ones are thousands of light-years away. The Ordovician extinction (~445M years ago) may record one. No nearby progenitor threatens us; this is science, not worry.

program.code:
# Impact energy estimator
import math
def impact_energy(diameter_m, velocity_kms, density=3000):
    r = diameter_m/2
    m = 4/3*math.pi*r**3*density
    E = 0.5*m*(velocity_kms*1000)**2
    return E/4.184e15  # kilotons TNT
for d, v in [(20,19),(50,20),(140,20),(1000,20)]:
    print(f"{d:>4}m at {v} km/s: {impact_energy(d,v):,.0f} kilotons")
